newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - C&W gets the man it wants.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - C&W gets the man it wants.

text.p: Cable and Wireless (C&W) on Friday brushed aside speculation that its landmark merger with three companies had run into obstacles and said it had got the man it wanted to run what will be to Britain's biggest cable firm.

In a long-awaited statement, C&W said it would appoint Graham Wallace chief executive of Cable and Wireless Communications, formed by merging C&W's Mercury unit, Nynex Corp's NYNEX CableComms Group, Bell Cablemedia Plc, and Videotron Holdings Plc.
"Graham Wallace is the one we wanted," C&W chief executive Richard Brown told Reuters in an interview.
"He is the first choice and we're delighted to get him."
With C&W planning to finalise the cable merger in spring, the lack of a chief executive at the new company had fuelled some speculation that a clash of cultures was hindering talks.

Although Brown conceded that the merger was complicated, he insisted: "That is not true...We have steering committees that are working on the merger work and operations. There's a great deal of activity and we really are right on track.
Brown, who will take the chair of the new company, said a finance director would be the next announcement.
"There is an exciting spirit of cooperation to bring this to reality," he said.

Alliances of this type often spell job cuts. But while Brown said he was not legally allowed to comment ahead of a planned listing in London and New York, he warned that the new company would "clearly" reap efficiencies.
"I cannot quantify what that is going to be, but we are working on that and we will achieve that. So we're very pleased with what is happening, as complicated as it is," he said.

Wallace, who brings television and satellite TV skills with him from previous jobs with BSkyB, will join C&W on February 1. He is currently a director at leisure and media group Granada Group. Cable and Wireless Communications, which will be well-placed to compete against dominant UK telecoms company British Telecommunications, will provide local, national and international data and mobile telecommunications with multi-channel television and Internet services.
The proposed merger was announced last October.
